status: Internal plan fixed after algebraic derivation, before any new numerical population calculation or replay. Existing unweighted endpoint results were already known. No external preregistration.
question: For a specified positive whole-utility scale, quantify the trade-off between compensated finite attainment and fixed-dimensional oracle variance along fixed row weights w(D)=D^(-r).
normalization: Each weighted loss divides by the original sample count. A single common positive normalization of the complete objective is permitted. Separate labelled and auxiliary weight normalization changes the finite objective.
pairing: Reuse every previous radial Gaussian design, choice, proxy and scale. r=0 must agree with the previous variable-scale status; r=1 must agree with previous constant-scale status. All new exponents and reverse transitions are retained.
primary_classifier: Residual feasibility with effective scale D^(1-r), using the exact recession identity.
independent_verifier: Reconstruct the original D-scaled design and the actual row-weighted logit objective; independently classify every criterion through its weighted attainable moment. Store all negative recession directions.
additional_checks: independent Gaussian integration for every population row
covariance log-moment derivatives and second-order cost
recession identity on fixed arbitrary designs, powers and directions
no replacement of weighted loss by a coefficient-equivalent virtual likelihood
excluded_claims: general optimality of intermediate power weights
population monotonicity implies nested finite-sample events
